 By David Fleming October 28 2026 - 1:02am By David Fleming October 28 2026 - 1:02am Save Share Things are looking up for Australia's Maya Joint, who beat the sixth seed in Tokyo. Photo: Matt Turner/AAP PHOTOS Maya Joint has made a mockery of the tennis rankings with an impressive display to uproot one of the top seeds at the Pan Pacific Open event in Tokyo.

 However, the American-born Aussie showed the numbers can't always be trusted as she powered past sixth seed and world No.16 Sorana Cirstea of Romania.
 Joint's impressive 6-3 7-6 (7-4) victory on Tuesday secured her a spot in the round of 16.
 It also continued her recent resurgence, after she made the final at last month's Korea Open in Seoul, where compatriot Kim Birrell claimed her first WTA title with a 6-4 6-2 win in the final.
 Joint's next opponent is Spanish world No.42 Cristina Bucsa, who beat France's Diane Parry 7-5 6-1 on Tuesday.
 And Joint isn't the only in-form Australian still in the main draw.
 On Monday, Talia Gibson, who recently reached the Singapore final, came through an all-Australian affair over qualifier Daria Kasatkina 6-0 7-5.
 Gibson powered through the first eight games in a row but was made to work hard to hold off the former world No.8 in the second set.
 Her reward is a round-of-16 clash with eight-seeded Aleandra Eala, of the Philippines.
 Talia Gibson won an all-Australian battle against Daria Kasatkina in Tokyo. (Lukas Coch/AAP PHOTOS) Eala won the battle of former US Open junior champions, easing past 17-year-old British wildcard Mika Stojsavljevic 6-1 6-2 in just 75 minutes.
 The popular Philippines player claimed the girls' title at Flushing Meadows in 2022, two years before Stojsavljevic lifted the trophy.
 The Tokyo event has been hit hard by injuries, with two of the tournament's biggest names withdrawing.
 Poland's Maja Chwalinska, the No.2 seed, and Switzerland's Belinda Benic, seeded fourth, both pulled out before the tournament kicked off.
 But home favourite Naomi Osaka is there and she defeated Italy's Jasmine Paolini 6-3 7-6 (7-4) hitting seven aces. There were also wins for Yulia Putinseva and Leylah Fernandez.
 Meanwhile, in the Guangzhou Open lost 6-2 6-2 to Austrian teenager Lilli Tagger to be 0-13 in singles this year. The 28-year age gap between Williams, 46, and Tagger, 18, is believed to be a record difference between opponents in a WTA Tour match.
 Williams created no break-point chances and Tagger took four of the 16 she had.
